fields.summary: sippy-dev MCP: sippy_serve reports server ready before HTTP API is available
fields.description:
The sippy_serve MCP tool reports the backend as running based on process detection (checking for existing sippy serve PIDs), not by verifying the HTTP API is actually accepting requests.

During local dev startup, {{go run ./cmd/sippy serve}} takes time to compile and initialize before the HTTP server binds. The MCP tool can detect the {{go run}} process and report "already running" with a listen address, even though the API isn't serving yet. This leads to a cascading failure:

# {{sippy_serve}} is called — {{go run}} starts compiling (takes 30-60+ seconds)
# Call is interrupted or MCP detects the process and reports ready
# {{sippy_ng_start}} is called — frontend starts on :3000
# User opens the app — frontend fetches {{/api/releases}} against a backend that isn't ready
# Fetch fails, app enters a degraded state, and navigating to component readiness crashes

*Fix:* After detecting or spawning the process, the tool should poll the HTTP endpoint (e.g. {{GET /api/releases}} or a lightweight health endpoint) before reporting ready. A timeout with a clear error message ("backend process started but API not responding") would also help.

*File:* mcp/sippy_dev/tools/sippy_serve.py (or wherever the MCP tool is implemented)

status.description: The work item is considered finished, the resolution is correct. work items which are closed can be reopened.
